title: Sound waves can make bubbles in water flash with light
body: Blast water with strong ultrasound and tiny bubbles repeatedly swell and then collapse violently. At the moment of collapse they give off brief flashes of light, an effect called sonoluminescence. The gas inside can briefly reach temperatures estimated at up to about 12,000 kelvin, though exactly how the light is made is still debated. Nature got there first: the snapping claw of the pistol shrimp makes a collapsing bubble that emits a faint flash.
